messages:
claire: Quick q — should we move cost/latency scoring into compile-time or keep it at runtime? thinking about scale + hot-reload complexity.
ashwin: We touched this in the RFC but didn't lock it. My vote is split: keep matchers/filters in compile-time, scoring in runtime. Matchers are stable and cheap to evaluate; scores need live telemetry.
jordan: +1. Static rules narrow candidate set, runtime scorer ranks candidates with live metrics. Makes hot-reload cheap because you only recompile matchers.
tim: Tradeoffs: runtime scoring adds per-request cost. If scoring is expensive we can batch or cache. Also need determinism for canaries — scoring must be reproducible or seedable.
sofia: Also think about tier normalization: how do we compare a dedicated GPU pool vs hosted multi-tenant? need normalized units so weight combination makes sense.
ashwin: Agreed. Proposal: compute per-tier percentiles (or z-scores) then combine. e.g. `score = w_latency * latency_rank + w_cost * cost_rank + w_region * region_penalty`. That keeps contributions comparable.
claire: Edge case: new tenant or new route with no telemetry. Fallbacks/prior expectations needed. How do we encode priors?
jordan: I sketched a tiny proto for priors: ```message CandidatePrior { string model_variant = 1; float expected_p90_latency_ms = 2; float cost_per_token = 3; }``` but we probably can't surface protos directly in the policy DSL. Could use an embedded JSON priors blob per tenant.
tim: Another design: provide a ScoreTransformer plugin interface at runtime. Adapters implement `ScoreTransformer.compute(metrics, tenant_meta, config)` -> float. This lets us swap heuristics or ML predictors without restacking the engine.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: rolling canary: policy-engine/v2 -> hosts 3/3 healthy, 0 errors.
sofia: Important fairness note: global normalization can be skewed by huge tenants. We should normalize on tenant or cohort when enough samples exist, else fallback to cohort/global.
ashwin: Hierarchical normalization makes sense: tenant-level if n>threshold else cohort-level else global. We'll need telemetry to track sample counts.
claire: Action items: Ashwin -> update RFC (compile/runtime split + ScoreTransformer API). Jordan -> draft priors JSON schema. Tim -> prototype normalization functions and perf numbers.
tim: I'll run a bench: target 200k rps, scoring budget ~50us per candidate; otherwise we need batching. Will post numbers by EOD.
jordan: tiny nit: fallback selection should be stable across retries — include a request-scoped random seed so A/B and retries are consistent.
claire: +1, and add an `explain` payload to return top factors (latency/cost/region_penalty) for debugging.
sofia: LGTM. small nit: prefer `region_penalty` to be additive (ease of reasoning) not multiplicative.
nashwin: Noted. I'll draft the PR with the API shape and example policy snippet.
claire: Thanks everyone — keeping this as follow-up for RFC update and a prototype before next architecture sync.
